pinterest.title: Engagement Ring Setting for an Active Lifestyle: 9 Settings Rated for Real Life
pinterest.description: Choosing an engagement ring setting for an active lifestyle? Ask four questions: how high the stone sits, what it can catch on, how much of its edge is covered and how much upkeep it needs. Our guide rates nine settings, from full bezel and flush to low claw, channel and bar, then covers stones, metals and ring care for sport and travel, including before a wedding abroad.

pinterest.title: Bezel Setting Engagement Ring: The Safest Choice for Active Hands
pinterest.description: A full bezel wraps a thin rim of metal right around the stone's edge. GIA rates it well for daily knocks and chipping, and with no claw tips to snag a glove or a jumper, it suits climbers, divers, chefs and anyone in gloves half the year. The trade-off: slightly less light than claws. See how it compares with eight other settings for an active lifestyle.

pinterest.title: Low Profile Engagement Ring Tips: Why Six Claws Beat Four
pinterest.description: Love the sparkle of claws but live an active life? Choose six claws over four: if one of four shears off the stone can fall out, while with six it is likely to stay put. Keep the head low so the stone takes fewer direct hits, and have the claws checked every six months, or at least yearly. Booking a check four to six weeks before you fly is a sensible rule of thumb.

slides: Ski lift, reef dive, long-haul flight. Which engagement ring setting survives all three?
Four tests for any setting: how high the stone sits, what it can catch on, how much of its edge is covered and how much upkeep it needs.
Full bezel: a metal rim right around the stone. Low snag risk and the highest protection, for a little less sparkle.
Flush setting: the stone sits level with the band. About as snag-free as a setting gets, best for smaller, durable stones.
Love claws? Choose six over four, keep the head low and have them checked every six months.
Tension, channel and bar settings can be hard or even impossible to resize. Confirm the size before you order.
Diving, climbing, skiing or gym day? Swap to a plain or flush-set band and keep the engagement ring safe.
Ring sorted and thinking about where? Tell us your date and guest list, or chat with a Wedded Advisor about a wedding abroad.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Most ring guides rank settings by looks. Ours asks what happens on a ski lift, a reef dive and a long-haul flight.

The right engagement ring setting for an active lifestyle comes down to four plain questions: how high the stone sits, what it can catch on, how much of its edge is covered, and how much looking after it needs.

A full bezel is the safest all-round choice for active hands. Flush settings are about as snag-free as it gets. If you love claws, choose six over four, keep the head low and book a check every six months.

Heading overseas? Pack your rings in your carry-on, never checked luggage, tell your insurer your travel dates, and book a setting check four to six weeks before you fly.

Our full guide rates nine settings, plus stones, metals and ring care for sport and travel. Link in bio.
